findings: FiniteHitting counts unhit demands as a 0/1 potential. Incidence counting over each set of size at least r supplies r*potential <= n*drop for some vertex. A positive potential then gives genuine strict progress, so the existing finite greedy run terminates and hits every family member.

The cardinality bound is the existing relative-progress doubling argument with block n/r+1 and Nat.log 2 |Q|+1 rounds, including empty Q. No independent random sample or probabilistic existence assumption is introduced.

pathSet and longPairs refer to the actual consistent canonical unit-cost shortest walks. Their support has hop length+1 vertices, since the chosen positive-length optimum is simple. HitsLong quantifies over the same Optimal predicate and uniqueness identifies it with the canonical walk.

Consistent optimal segments establish every length-r interval contains a sample. Strong induction on walk length with the first interval starting at index1 gives positive progress, and creates actual sampled-kernel edges of original distance at most r+1.

For a longer original pair, samples in the first and last length-r intervals have ordered positions; prefix and suffix give the access bounds, and the middle optimal segment gives reachability in the actual sampled relation. The constructed Kernel field uses R=2r and L=2r+2, valid though the individual estimates are sometimes stronger.
sampleKernel supplies every field without an external kernel-existence premise, and |longPairs|<=n^2 yields the stated deterministic sample-size bound. The r=0 and empty-family regimes are included.
scope: The construction works for arbitrary finite directed graphs; no DAG assumption is used.
The proofs use the established globally consistent unit-cost Optimal walks, not the invalid source-rebased normalized optimality.
These are noncomputable finite constructions with mathematical cardinality and hop guarantees. No host-runtime complexity is claimed.
The original-paper high-target parameter balancing and resulting all-regime asymptotic rate remain separate.
This review binds exact local source hashes; no compilation or kernel replay was performed by this reviewer.
